description: We are a multidisciplinary team driven by technology and Earth science, consisting of ICT engineers and one environmental engineer. We combine advanced software development, geospatial data processing, and environmental expertise to build innovative solutions for the Earth systems trends challenge.
summary: AndesSAR (Earth Trends) is an interactive web platform and persistent geospatial repository designed to monitor territorial transformations such as deforestation and agricultural expansion. Our solution addresses this challenge using a robust cloud-backed workflow powered by PostGIS. Users can upload custom GeoTIFF raster datasets (up to 500 MiB) with metadata like capture dates and context notes, or explore pre-loaded multi-year land-cover maps of Ecuador spanning from 2021 to 2025. Within the Geoportal, the system enables users to inspect exact pixel coordinates, delimit custom rectangular areas, or filter statistics by single and multiple provinces. Furthermore, the dedicated comparison module allows users to contrast two processed maps side-by-side or play smooth animated transitions to quantify surface and ecological changes over time. This project is important because it delivers scalable, frequent environmental monitoring in vast or inaccessible regions where traditional field surveys fall short. By democratizing access to transparent geospatial data and bilingual usability (English and Spanish), our platform empowers researchers, regional planners, and institutions to make informed decisions for sustainable land management.
details: AndesSAR (Earth Trends), developed by team Kroma, is an interactive web platform powered by PostGIS and cloud infrastructure (Render) that allows users to upload, visualize, and analyze multi-year GeoTIFF satellite land-cover datasets across Ecuador without requiring specialized desktop GIS software. By offering pre-loaded historical catalogs (2021–2025), pixel-level inspection, province-based area calculations (km2), and parallel or animated multitemporal comparisons, the project democratizes access to Earth observation data and improves environmental monitoring of deforestation and ecosystem shifts. Creatively bridging complex geospatial processing with a clean, bilingual (English/Spanish) browser interface, our team carefully balanced server performance, upload safeguards (up to 500 MiB), and strict spatial accuracy (zero interpolation on valid grid pixels) to deliver a transparent, high-impact decision-making tool for researchers, planners, and students alike.
